# Baja Mineral Explorer

> Satellite-based mineral prospecting atlas for the San Quintín Municipio,
> Baja California, Mexico. Three surveyed targets, 36 GPS field pins,
> 14 documented Cu–Fe epithermal workings, sub-meter imagery (0.37–1.03 m/px).

## What this site is
An independent desk-study atlas combining:
- Sentinel-2 2020 cloudless composite (10 m, 13 bands, open, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
- Esri World Imagery (0.37–1.03 m/px sub-meter tiles, research use)
- SRTM-derived 10 m DEM (USGS, public domain) for slope/aspect/hillshade
- SGM Carta Geológico-Minera El Aguajito H11-B85, 1:50,000 (2009) geology

## Key coordinates
- T1 Arroyo San Isidro: 29.903605, -115.383656 (score 5.4/10) — pale alteration patches on an N–S relay drainage, ~332 m
- T2 Cerro la Turquesa: 30.048522, -115.236173 (score 6.3/10) — km-scale pale argillic mass ~1 km W, NE–SW lineament ~1 km E, turquoise-mining toponym, 740 m hill
- T3 Cerro la Palmita: 30.025725, -115.286885 (score 5.5/10) — ridge between T1/T2, steepest terrain (30% area >15° slope), 800 m
- Documented Cu–Fe belt (La Turquesa zona mineralizada, SGM 2009): 14 abandoned workings between 30.05–30.15° N, 115.34–115.52° W (El Cardonal — documented turquoise; San Martín — chrysocolla/azurite/malachite; La Turquesa core; El Hormiguero; La Bonita; 5 Minas; El Sacrificio; Josefina; Santa Martha; Santa Lucía; La Víbora; El Moro)

## Method
Per coordinate the pipeline computes a B/R blue-shift proxy (Fe-oxide depletion /
clay-calcite indicator), HSV surface classes (vegetation / soil / pale-tone /
bright crust / shadow), and DEM-derived slope, aspect, hillshade and drainage
transects, then cross-references the SGM 1:50,000 sheet. Full-band mode (free
Earthdata login) adds NDVI, ferric-iron, clay and carbonate indices at 30 m.
Google/Bing data is used only via official APIs (Earth Engine, Bing Maps Imagery
API); no tile-server scraping.

## Data downloads
- /maps/PIN_POINTS.csv — all 36 field pins (lat/lon, type, field action)
- /maps/mine_inventory_elaguajito.csv — 14 documented SGM workings
- /maps/*.jpg — pin sheets (1.03 m/px), 0.52 m/px pale-mass detail, 4×4 km field sheets, corridor overview

## Disclaimers
Desk study only — not investment, drilling, or legal advice. Mexican mining is
governed by the Ley Minera (2023 reform): concessions only by public tender,
prohibited in ANPs and water-stressed zones, prior consultation required.
Not affiliated with SGM, CONAGUA, or the Government of Mexico.
